title: Calculate linear magnification (mirrors)

hook.scenario: Zoom in feature se aap photo ko 2x ya 3x bada kar dete ho.
hook.question: Physics mein ek mirror kisi object ko kitna bada ya chota karta hai, usko numbers mein kaise napte hain?

mental_model.intuition: Magnification (m) bata-ta hai ki image, object se kitne guna badi (ya choti) hai.
mental_model.description: Agar m = 2 hai, toh image object se double height ki hai. Agar m = 0.5 hai, toh image aadhi height ki reh gayi. Iska sign (+/-) yeh bata-ta hai ki image seedhi (erect) hai ya ulti (inverted).

explanation:
Magnification (m) simply height of image (h') aur height of object (h) ka ratio hota hai. Formula mein ise likhte hain: m = h' / h.

Ek doosra tareeqa bhi hai magnification nikalne ka, jo image distance (v) aur object distance (u) se juda hota hai. Mirrors ke liye yeh relation hai: m = -v / u. Aap in dono ko jod kar ek super-formula bana sakte ho: m = h'/h = -v/u. Numerical solve karte time hum aksar issi ka cross-multiplication karke unknown values nikalte hain.

Magnification ka sign (+ ya -) bohot saari kahani bolta hai. Agar 'm' negative (-) hai, iska matlab image real and inverted hai (kyunki ulte image ki height negative hoti hai). Agar 'm' positive (+) hai, toh image virtual and erect hogi.

Value ka number (magnitude) size batata hai. Agar |m| > 1 (jaise +3 ya -2), image magnified (badi) hai. Agar |m| < 1 (jaise +0.5 ya -0.2), image diminished (choti) hai. Agar m = 1 ya -1, toh size equal hai.

key_points.title: Height Formula
key_points.detail: m = h' / h (where h' is image height, h is object height).

key_points.title: Sign Meaning
key_points.detail: m is negative for real, inverted images. m is positive for virtual, erect images.

worked_example.problem: A concave mirror produces a magnification of -3. What does this mean about the image?

steps.math: Sign is (-). So image is Real and Inverted.
Magnitude is 3. So image is Enlarged (3 times the object).

worked_example.answer: The image is real, inverted, and 3 times larger than the object.

worked_example.problem: Find the magnification of a mirror if an object placed at u = -10 cm forms an image at v = +5 cm.

steps.narration: Distances wala magnification formula use karein.

common_mistakes.title: Missing the minus sign in the formula
common_mistakes.explanation: Formula m = -v/u hai. Students kabhi kabhi minus lagana bhool jate hain aur sirf v/u use kar lete hain. -v/u mirrors ke liye hai, +v/u lenses ke liye.

recall_questions.q: What is the formula for magnification of a mirror in terms of object and image distance?
If magnification m is positive, is the image real or virtual?
What is the formula for magnification of a mirror in terms of v and u?

oa_questions.question: A spherical mirror produces a magnification of -1 on a screen placed at a distance of 50 cm from the mirror. Write the type of mirror.
oa_questions.approach: m = -1 means it's a real, inverted image of the same size. Only a concave mirror can form a real image.

oa_questions.question: A mirror has m = +1.5. Is it a concave or convex mirror?
oa_questions.answer: Concave, because it forms a magnified virtual image.
oa_questions.approach: Convex mirrors always form diminished images (m < 1), so it must be concave.
